problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}16 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ shown above. If the general solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of  $a+\frac{b}{c}?$

feedback.problem:
Find the solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{2}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {1}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {1}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-12 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the matrix on the left-hand side is invertible, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & ={[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5\cdot 2-1\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}-18 \\ 18\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
